problems.title: Divide by the highest power
problems.question: Find lim as x→∞ of (2x³+3x²)/x³.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: The second term tends to zero, so the limit is 2.

problems.title: Sum an arithmetic progression before taking a limit
problems.question: Find lim as n→∞ of [5+9+13+…+(4n+1)]/n².
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: There are n terms. Their sum is n(5+4n+1)/2=2n²+3n.
Divide by n² to get 2+3/n, whose limit is 2.

problems.title: The sine limit with a changed argument
problems.question: Find lim as x→0 of 2sin(7x)/(3x).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: Write the expression as (14/3)·sin(7x)/(7x). The last factor tends to 1.

problems.title: Which shapes can be cone sections?
problems.question: Among right triangle,circle,equilateral triangle,isosceles triangle,scalene triangle,obtuse triangle,how many cannot be a cone section?
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: A plane through a right circular cone’s apex meets two equal-length generators, so any nondegenerate triangular section is isosceles.
steps: A plane parallel to the base gives a circle. Apex sections can be equilateral,right isosceles or obtuse isosceles for suitable cone openings.
A scalene triangle is impossible. Thus exactly one of the listed shape types cannot occur.
problems.note: The question is interpreted as asking which shapes can occur among right circular cones. For one fixed cone, its opening also restricts the possible apex angles.

problems.title: Distance from a point to a line
problems.question: Find the distance from (1,3) to 3x−2y=4.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: Use A=3,B=−2,C=−4. The numerator is |3−6−4|=7 and denominator √13.

problems.title: An exponential limit
problems.question: Find lim as x→+∞ of [(x+2)/(x−3)]^x.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: Put t=x−3. The expression becomes (1+5/t)^(t+3).
The factor with exponent t tends to e⁵ and the extra factor (1+5/t)³ tends to 1.

problems.title: A one-sided arctangent limit
problems.question: Find lim as x→1+ of arctan[1/(1−x)].
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: Approaching from the right makes 1−x a small negative number. Its reciprocal tends to −∞.

problems.title: Cancel factorials first
problems.question: Find lim as n→∞ of [(n+5)!−(n+2)!]/[n³(n+2)!].
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: After cancellation, divide [(n+5)(n+4)(n+3)−1] by n³.
The numerator is a cubic with leading coefficient 1, so the ratio tends to 1.

problems.title: Use the sector angle of a cone net
problems.question: A cone has lateral area 20 and net-sector angle 72°. Find total area.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: $\theta l=2\pi r$, with θ in radians; $L=\pi rl$, $S=L+\pi r^2$.
steps: Since 72° is one fifth of a full turn, r/l=1/5.
Therefore πr²=(r/l)L=20/5=4. Add the base to the lateral area: 20+4=24.

problems.title: A cone frustum around a sphere
problems.question: A frustum tangent to a radius-6 sphere has slant height 13. Find lateral area.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: The axial trapezoid is tangent to the sphere’s great circle, so R+r=l=13.
Consequently L=π·13·13=169π. Its height is twice the sphere radius,12, consistent with |R−r|=5.

problems.title: Differentiate a cube of a sine
problems.question: For f(x)=sin³(4x+π/3),find f′(π/12).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: Here u′=4 and u(π/12)=2π/3.
Thus f′=12sin²u cosu, and the required value is 12·(3/4)·(−1/2)=−9/2.

problems.title: Take logarithms in a power limit
problems.question: Find lim as x→0+ of (1/x)^(sinx).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: For positive Y, $\ln Y=\sin x\ln(1/x)$; also x ln(1/x)→0.
steps: Rewrite the logarithm as [sinx/x]·[x ln(1/x)]. The factors tend to 1 and 0, respectively.
The logarithm tends to zero, so the original positive expression tends to e⁰=1.

problems.title: Apply the chain rule to a polynomial cube
problems.question: Find f′(1) for f(x)=(3x⁴−10x+8)³+x⁵.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: At x=1 the inner polynomial is 1 and its derivative is 2. Therefore f′(1)=3·1²·2+5=11.

problems.title: Rotate a regular hexagon about a long diagonal
problems.question: Find surface area when a regular side-a hexagon rotates about a longest diagonal.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: Rotation produces two cones and a cylinder, all with radius $r=\sqrt3a/2$; $S=2\pi rl+2\pi rh$.
steps: The two sloping sides of the upper half each have length a, generating cone lateral surfaces. The horizontal middle side has length a, generating a cylinder.
Thus both cone slant lengths and the cylinder height equal a. The total exposed surface is 2πra+2πra=4πra=2√3πa².
The common circular joins are internal and add no exposed area.

problems.title: Area from two coordinate vectors
problems.question: Find area of the triangle A(3,5),B(7,8),C(6,1).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: Take AB=(4,3),AC=(3,−4). Their determinant is −16−9=−25.
Area is half its absolute value: 25/2.

problems.title: Bound an oscillating sequence
problems.question: Find lim as n→∞ of √n cosn/(n+1).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: The upper bound tends to zero because it behaves like 1/√n. The squeeze theorem gives limit zero.

problems.title: Chain rule for an arctangent and square root
problems.question: Find f′(1) for f(x)=arctan√(4x−1).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.

problems.title: Deleting the last two digits of squares
problems.question: Delete the final two digits from 1000²,1001²,1002²,… . What is the longest initial arithmetic progression?
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: For k=0,…,9,the floor term is zero. These first ten terms have difference 20.
At k=10 the floor term becomes 1,so the next difference is 21 and the arithmetic progression stops.

problems.title: The smaller angle between two lines
problems.question: Find the angle between y=5−3x and y=2x−1.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: The slopes are −3 and 2, so tanθ=|5/(−5)|=1. Therefore θ=π/4.
problems.note: Two intersecting lines also form the supplementary angle 3π/4, which is another listed choice. The standard “angle between lines” means the smaller angle.

problems.title: Minimise four distances using the diagonals
problems.question: Find K minimising KA+KB+KC+KD for A(0,0),B(5,1),C(6,3),D(−1,4).
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: $KA+KC\ge AC$, $KB+KD\ge BD$. Equality holds when K lies on both diagonal segments.
steps: Thus t=7/12,s=1/4, both within [0,1]. The diagonals intersect at K=(7/2,7/4), attaining the lower bound AC+BD.

problems.title: Fill removable holes continuously
problems.question: For x≠±1 let f(x)=(x⁴−x²)/(x²−1); define f(1)=log₃a,f(−1)=√b. If f is continuous everywhere,find a+b.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: $x^4-x^2=x^2(x^2-1)$, so f(x)=x² away from the holes.
steps: Both limiting values at ±1 are 1. Therefore log₃a=1 gives a=3, and √b=1 gives b=1. Their sum is 4.

problems.title: Choose the smallest root for the subtracted term
problems.question: The roots of f′(x)=0 are a,b,c,where f=x⁴/4+2x³+(3/2)x²−10x. Maximise a−b+c.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
steps: The three roots sum to −6. Hence a−b+c=(a+b+c)−2b=−6−2b.
Make b the smallest root,−5,to maximise the result: −6+10=4.

problems.title: A self-repeating logarithm
problems.question: Let x=log_(log_(log_…27)27)27 and y=log₂8. Which listed value can x+y equal?
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: If the infinite nested expression has value x, self-similarity gives $x=\log_x27$, or $x\ln x=\ln27$.
steps: A logarithm base must be positive and unequal to 1. Since the outer logarithm of 27 equals its base, the value must exceed 1.
On x>1,the function x ln x is strictly increasing. x=3 works because 3³=27,so it is the unique possible value.
Also y=3. Therefore x+y=6.
problems.note: This is the usual interpretation of an infinite nested logarithm as a convergent self-repeating value; a finite nesting depth would need to be specified separately.

problems.title: A sphere tangent outside a cone
problems.question: A cone’s axial section is equilateral with side6. A sphere touches its lateral surface and base plane at a point 4 from the axis. Find cone-area/sphere-area.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: The cone has R=3,l=6,h=3√3. In an axial plane the relevant side is $\sqrt3x+z-3\sqrt3=0$.
steps: Let the sphere radius be ρ. Its centre is (4,ρ),above the base; its distance from the cone-side line must equal ρ.
Thus (4√3+ρ−3√3)/2=ρ, giving ρ=√3. The perpendicular foot lies on the actual cone side.
Cone area=πR(R+l)=27π. Sphere area=4πρ²=12π. Their ratio is 27/12=9/4.

problems.title: Four mutually tangent spheres on one plane
problems.question: Two spheres of radius R and two of radius r are mutually tangent and tangent to one plane. Find larger/smaller surface-area ratio.
problems.idea: Simplify the expression or reduce the geometry to a familiar formula.
formulas: The horizontal separation of tangent spheres of radii u,v on the same side of a plane is $2\sqrt{uv}$.
steps: The equal-radius pairs have projected separations 2R and 2r. Every cross-pair separation is 2√(Rr).
Both small projections are equidistant from the two large projections, so they lie on the perpendicular bisector. The small pair is symmetric about the large-pair midpoint.
A right triangle of half-diagonals gives R²+r²=4Rr. Thus R/r=2+√3 (taking R>r).
Surface areas scale as radius squared: (R/r)²=(2+√3)²=7+4√3.
